title: Coupled rate-latency SLA and error budget playbook for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Priya Desai
description: Define a practical SLA model for Dedicated capacity that ties guaranteed token/rate commitments to latency bands, includes an explicit error budget calculation, and prescribes contractual remediation and crediting behavior. Scope: (1) SLA metric definitions (coupled rate + latency quantiles), (2) error budget math and burn windows, (3) autoscaler interlock rules that trigger credits versus transient mitigation, (4) customer notice and dispute process, and (5) sample contract clauses and operational runbooks for incident response and credit computation.
acceptance_criteria: SLA spec with unambiguous metric, measurement window, and collection method reviewed by Reliability and Legal
Error budget formula validated against 6 months of synthetic and production traces; example computations for 3 customer profiles (small, mid, large)
Autoscale interlock defined: clear thresholds for temporary throttling, emergency autoscale, and credit eligibility
Set of contract language snippets approved by Legal for inclusion in Dedicated contracts and addenda
Instrumented dashboards (per-customer) showing live SLI, consumption of error budget, and burn-rate projections
measurement_plan: Primary SLIs: 1) Guaranteed Serve Rate (tokens/minute or requests/sec) measured per-customer across committed capacity pools; 2) Latency quantiles (p50/p90/p99) for committed request class. Measurement window: rolling 1-hour with daily and 30-day aggregations. Error budget: compute as percentage of time the combined constraint fails within the 30-day window, weighted by severity of latency band. Burn-rate: normalized units combining rate shortfall and latency degradations. Data sources: Console request traces, gateway metrics, and the serving runtime's token counters. Aggregation and disputes: retain raw traces for 90 days for audit and dispute resolution.
contract_language_snippets: Service Commitment: Provider will maintain a Guaranteed Serve Rate (GSR) of X tokens/minute for the Customer's Dedicated Pool and will ensure that >= 95% of produced responses meet the p90 latency target of Y ms over a rolling 30-day window.

Error Budget and Credits: An Error Budget is defined as the permitted fraction of non‑conforming minutes within a 30‑day window. If the Error Budget is exceeded, Provider will credit the Customer according to the Credit Schedule below. Credits are computed pro rata on the monthly Dedicated Capacity fee and will not exceed Z% per billing period.

Autoscale Interlock: Temporary degradations that are automatically mitigated by Provider-managed emergency autoscale are eligible for reduced or no credit if they meet the mitigation and notification criteria. A manual remediation trigger or failure to autoscale within the defined time window qualifies for full credit consideration.

Notification and Dispute Resolution: Provider will publish incidents to the Customer portal within T minutes of detection and provide a preliminary impact estimate. Customers have 30 days to open a dispute with attached trace IDs for audit. Final credit adjustments will be made within one billing cycle after resolution.
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (pilot): Offer the coupled SLA to 3 strategic customers on Dedicated v1 pools for a 60-day pilot to validate measurement and credit computation; collect feedback on wording and edge cases.

Phase 2: After pilot sign-off, bake SLA into new contracts and provide an opt-in migration path for existing Dedicated customers. Update Console with per-customer SLI tiles and error budget burn indicators.
Billing: Billing team to add a dedicated line item for SLA credits; credits to be computed automatically but require manual Legal sign-off for amounts above a threshold.
Comm plan: Customer success to prepare FAQ and runbooks. Sales to include a one-pager describing the coupled rate-latency approach and what customers should test during onboarding.
decisions: Couple rate and latency into a single SLA construct rather than separate SLAs to reduce ambiguity when rate throttling causes latency improvements or degradations.
Use rolling 30-day windows as primary contractual period to balance transient spikes against sustained regressions.
Define error budget in normalized burn units (combining rate shortfalls and latency band violations) to provide a single signal for operational response and credit calculation.

Autoscale that restores service within the agreed remediation timeframe will reduce the credit amount; this creates an incentive for rapid mitigation while protecting customers for prolonged failures.
